draft.title: Initiatives for healthy eating
card: Dietary Guidelines

The Australian Dietary Guidelines are evidence-based advice on what and how much to eat for good health. They are written for the general population and are used by health professionals and policy makers.
Guide to Healthy Eating
The Australian Guide to Healthy Eating is a visual model that turns the guidelines into a plate. It shows the proportions of the five food groups to eat, with a small place for foods to limit.
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Guide

The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Guide to Healthy Eating is a separate guide with its own artwork. It reflects culture, including traditional foods, and the foods and settings that matter to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities.
All three promote better diets through education. They help people see what a healthy diet looks like, but they do not control what food people buy or eat.
draft.remember: Guidelines give the advice. The guides turn it into pictures people can use, including one for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.

a.q: What is the main purpose of the Australian Guide to Healthy Eating?
opts: To show visually the proportions of food groups to eat
To set legal limits on the sugar in packaged foods
To list the foods each person must eat every day
To replace the Australian Dietary Guidelines entirely
a.why: The guide turns the dietary guidelines into a picture of the food groups in proportion. It does not set laws or rules for individuals, and it is built on the guidelines rather than replacing them.
a.clue: Think about what the word guide and the plate image show.

b.q: A health worker at an Aboriginal community-controlled service in Victoria wants a resource that suits her community's culture and food traditions. Which initiative is the best fit?
opts: The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Guide
The Australian Guide to Healthy Eating
The Australian Dietary Guidelines
A food company's own healthy eating advertising
b.why: The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Guide to Healthy Eating is made to reflect culture and traditional foods. The general guide and guidelines are for the whole population and are not designed around one culture. Company advertising is not a health initiative of this kind.
b.clue: Which one was made for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples?

a.best: To show visually the proportions of food groups to eat

b.best: The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Guide

card: Dietary Guidelines

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Guide

The Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Guide to Healthy Eating is based on the same guidelines and the same five food groups. Its artwork and food examples reflect culture, including traditional foods and the settings that matter to communities.

b.q: Lena, a health worker, compares the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Guide to Healthy Eating with the general Australian guide. What is the main difference?
opts: Its artwork and food examples reflect culture
It is built on a different set of food groups
It replaces the dietary guidelines for these communities
It sets legal rules on what communities can buy
b.why: Both guides are based on the same dietary guidelines and five food groups, so the difference is in the artwork and food examples, which reflect culture and traditional foods. It is tempting to think the food groups change, but they do not. Neither guide replaces the guidelines or controls what people buy.
